drills.q: Rewrite 'Would you use an AI flashcard generator?' into two compliant interview questions.
drills.a: 'Tell me about the last time you made flashcards — walk me through it step by step' (episode) and 'What's the most you've ever done to fix that part of studying?' (workaround/receipts). Past behavior, no embedded solution.

drills.q: Compute the opportunity score: importance 9.1, satisfaction 2.4. And for importance 4.3, satisfaction 6.8?
drills.a: 9.1 x (10-2.4) = 69.2 -> build-worthy target (important AND miserable). 4.3 x (10-6.8) = 13.8 -> kill: unimportant regardless of satisfaction.

drills.q: Your smoke page converts cold traffic at 0.8%. What do you conclude and do?
drills.a: Below the ~1-2% floor, so demand as framed is dead — but check the framing confound first: if a sibling value proposition converted materially better (e.g., 9%), copy/framing was the problem and you pivot to the winner; if all framings fail, kill within a week at ~$200 cost instead of two quarters.

drills.q: Users praise your prototype enthusiastically in every interview but usage after launch is near zero. Explain with the four forces.
drills.a: Praise is pull only. Switching requires push evidenced by workarounds, credible pull, low anxiety, and low habit cost. Habit + anxiety beat polite pull: users stay with painful-but-known tools. Fix by measuring push pre-build (receipts), then reducing anxiety (reversibility, imports, trust signals).

drills.q: Design a 2-week discovery plan for AI hints in a practice tool, with two kill conditions.
drills.a: Days 1-2 telemetry/ticket mining for stuck-signals; days 3-6 six Mom-Test interviews on last stuck-episode; days 7-8 opportunity scoring; days 9-14 Wizard-of-Oz hints manually for 10-15 learners. Kill conditions e.g.: fewer than half report active workarounds; Oz hints don't lift next-attempt success >=15%.

drills.q: A stakeholder wants to survey 500 users instead of 8 interviews. When is each right, in what order?
drills.a: Interviews discover unknown options/mechanisms; surveys size prevalence across KNOWN options. Sequence: interview first to generate the answer space, then survey to size it. A big survey of leading questions industrializes bias.

drills.q: Two distinct solutions under one opportunity both failed their experiments. What now?
drills.a: Prune the opportunity itself: two independent failures suggest the opportunity lacks pull rather than bad execution. Slide up the tree, re-interview around the parent outcome, or reallocate to a higher-scoring sibling branch.

drills.q: How would you detect fabricated episodes from incentive-driven survey-taker recruits?
drills.a: Screen with open-ended past-behavior questions ('walk me through the last time...') where fabricators run out of specifics fast; cross-check dates/tools/details; prefer in-product triggered recruits who verifiably did the behavior recently.

drills.q: An LLM persona panel says 70% of students would adopt your study-buddy. What is this evidence worth?
drills.a: Zero evidentiary weight for validation — synthetic respondents have no causal link to real demand. Its only legitimate use is prioritizing which real interviews to run first or stress-testing question design. Citing it as validation is a red flag.

drills.q: Your team has run discovery for three cycles without shipping anything testable. Diagnose and prescribe.
drills.a: Process has replaced the goal (procrastination-by-process). Prescribe Torres-style cadence guard: weekly touchpoints, a decision artifact every cycle, and force the cheapest ladder test this week; if the tree keeps growing while nothing behavioral gets tested, cap total discovery timebox and require a flagged experiment before more interviews.
